pr_title: Allow conversions between compatible array types
pr_body:

Fixes #80586
pr_comments: I don't think the linked issue is correct, and thus the solution doesn't look right to me. (I didn't review it in detail though.)

I see. It seems the issue is not about conversions but whether an array has the expected or compatible element type so it can be passed to a function? If so, is it possible (or safe) to implement such a feature?

This is incorrect. You just removed the check in the static analyzer and GDScript runtime, but didn't solve the "problem", including in the core. The array type is not just the variable type, it is the type of an object in memory (because arrays are passed by reference). This restriction is needed to prevent the following:

![](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/47700418/0aa563ac-c360-43d0-a265-c9598d7536ea)

```gdscript
var a: Array[Node2D] = []
var b: Array[Node] = a # Now b refers to the same array as a.
b.append(Node.new()) # This is correct for b, but not for a!
print(a[0]) # Node
```

Thanks for the detailed explanation and advice from @dalexeev and others. Looks like this solution is unfeasible. Feel free to tell me what can be done or close this PR if no further discussion or action is needed.

> Looks like this solution is unfeasible. Feel free to tell me what can be done or close this PR if no further discussion or action is needed.

I think this can't be implemented in a simple way, unfortunately. In theory, we could allow compatible types to be read-only referenced if we added the `write`/`read` attributes to the type system, see https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/discussions/7364#discussioncomment-6576975. But I think that first we should reach a consensus in the discussion before opening a PR.

We definitely have issues with typed arrays that need to be resolved after we reach a consensus in the [discussion](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/discussions/7364).

Unfortunately, this PR doesn't look correct. Probably the correct solution to the #80586 problem would be [`read` parameter](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/discussions/7364#discussioncomment-6576975), [typed array constructor](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/71336) or something else.

Thanks for the contribution nonetheless!

issue_context.title: Functions accept typed arrays and cannot inherit conversions
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.2 dev3

### System information

Win10 Vulkan

### Issue description

```gdscript
extends Node2D

class A:
    func say()->void:
        print('A')

class B extends A:
    func say()->void:
        print('B')
		
func test(a:A)->void:
    a.say()
	
func test_arr(a:Array[A])->void:
    for _a in a:
        _a.say()

func _ready() -> void:
    test(B.new())
    var _b:Array[B]=[B.new(),B.new()]
    # Implicit type conversion,run error
    test_arr(_b)
    # Explicit type conversion
    test_arr(_b as Array[A]) 
	
    #only stupid manual conversion
    var _a:Array[A]=[]
    for i in _b:
        _a.append(i)

    test_arr(_a)


```

### Steps to reproduce

see description

### Minimal reproduction project

None
comments:
I don't think this issue is correct. Arrays are passed by reference, so they cannot be "converted". A new array must be created, which can lead to large memory consumption in case of large arrays. Also, element types must be **equal**, supertypes are not supported (because there is no read-only attribute in the type system).

What you perceive as a conversion is just a non-obvious behavior that we added for convenience. This only works for literals and constant expressions. We treat an untyped literal as typed, depending on the context. We should probably add a warning about this after we add [typed array constructor](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/71336).

See also godotengine/godot-proposals#7364 and [documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_basics.html#typed-arrays):

![](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/47700418/20055ddf-8f4b-4dbc-83e6-2bc13b26e8d3)

Maybe this is not a bug, but it is definitely a big flaw in the type system in terms of usage. At least there are methods or functions that support conversion, or syntactic sugar, otherwise it would be too stupid and boring to convert manually.

> At least there are methods or functions that support conversion, or syntactic sugar, otherwise it would be too stupid and boring to convert manually.

Instead of a loop:

> ```gdscript
>     #only stupid manual conversion
>     var _a:Array[A]=[]
>     for i in _b:
>         _a.append(i)
> 
>     test_arr(_a)
> ```

You can use the [`assign()`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_array.html#class-array-method-assign) method:

```gdscript
    var _a: Array[A] = []
    _a.assign(_b)
    test_arr(_a)
```

After #71336 you will be able to do:

```gdscript
    test_arr(Array[A](_b))
```

looks good, #71336 more in line with my expectations.

Thanks for the clarification.

review_comments: This is not an error, element types must be equal, supertypes are not supported. I have a [draft](https://github.com/dalexeev/godot/blob/1b596113a112e99fc3769cc9afa6485c81ed1e6c/modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp#L5084-L5092) with the `is_type_compatible()` refactoring in which I added a comment about it.
